name: Commander graveyard hate (Rest in Peace, Bojuka Bog, Scavenging Ooze)
description: A Commander opponent whose plan is to switch your graveyard off: Rest in Peace on turn 2, a Bojuka Bog land drop, Scavenging Ooze grinding the yard, Grafdigger's Cage against reanimation. Teaches which lines survive graveyard hate (drain loops and outlet-plus-payoff engines do; recursion and reanimator lines do not) and when to answer the hate piece instead of advancing your own board.

turns.boardSummary: 1 land; Leyline of the Void was in the opening hand and is already on the battlefield

events.note: Leyline: if it is in the opening hand it begins the game on the battlefield (CR 103.6). Cards that would go to your graveyard from anywhere are exiled instead.
events.breakPoint: Decision point: before the first draw, look at your line. 'Dies' means put into a graveyard from the battlefield (CR 700.4); with Leyline your creatures are exiled instead, so they never die and death triggers never fire. Aristocrats needs this Leyline gone before the engine matters.

turns.boardSummary: Rest in Peace: both graveyards exiled, all future cards exiled instead

events.note: When it enters, exile all graveyards; afterwards cards go to exile instead. Redundant with Leyline, and that is the point: two pieces means one removal spell is not enough.
events.breakPoint: Enchantment removal on Rest in Peace is worth a turn; do not spend it while Leyline is still there. Lines that never touch the graveyard (Exquisite Blood + Sanguine Bond, combat, storm) are unaffected.

turns.boardSummary: Bojuka Bog played: any graveyard you rebuilt is exiled again

events.note: Enters tapped; when it enters, exile target player's graveyard. A land, so it dodges creature and enchantment removal entirely.

turns.boardSummary: Scavenging Ooze and Grafdigger's Cage: no creature can enter from a graveyard

events.note: Creature cards in graveyards and libraries can't enter the battlefield; players can't cast spells from graveyards or libraries. Reanimation and flashback are shut off.
events.breakPoint: Decision point: with Cage down, a reanimator line is dead until it leaves. Pivot to casting the threat from hand, or to the line that does not need the graveyard.

events.note: Every green mana exiles a card from a graveyard and grows the Ooze. It also gains them life.

turns.boardSummary: Ooze is a 6/6 from eating graveyards and attacks every turn
Hate pieces still up; the Ooze keeps attacking. If your line needed the graveyard, you needed an answer by now.

events.note: Decision point: a hate deck wins by making your plan impossible, not by racing. Count your outs that remove BOTH Leyline and Rest in Peace, or switch to the line that ignores them.
